verdict.line: You win if you fight at Q/E range and punish Rupture whiffs or overextensions with your level 6 execute; you lose if you auto-trade in melee where Vorpal Spikes stacks up or let Cho rack up enough Feast kills to outscale you late.

brief.thesis: Urgot's entire kit (Q 800 range, E 475 range, W 490 range) out-ranges everything Cho'Gath has except Rupture, so this lane is decided by whether Urgot stays at the edge of Vorpal Spikes range (40) instead of trading autos point-blank. The data backs this: Urgot holds the lane advantage and the solo-kill edge, but the overall 50% head-to-head over 92 games reflects Cho'Gath clawing back relevance once Feast stacking inflates his max HP.

theirWindow.when: Rupture lands or Feast is off cooldown
theirWindow.what: Cho'Gath's Q (Rupture, 950 range, 9s cooldown) pops you up and slows, setting up free Vorpal Spikes autos if you walk forward afterward; his R (Feast, 175 range, 60s cooldown) is a true-damage eat that can delete low-HP minions, jungle camps, or you if you're caught in melee range.

yourWindow.when: After he lands or whiffs Rupture
yourWindow.what: His Q is now down for 9 seconds and his only ranged tool is gone — step back in to 800 range and chip with Q (Corrosive Charge) and E (Disdain), letting Echoing Flames and W (Purge) finish the trade from 490 range, well outside his Vorpal Spikes radius.

start.why: The measured pick (89.5% pick rate, 47.1% WR over 102 games) — the extra sustain and early AD let you win autoattack trades at the edges of his Vorpal Spikes range without burning summoner sustain early.

boots.why: Lower pick rate but the better measured result (48.5% WR vs Mercury's Treads' 38.8%) — flat reduction on basic attack damage directly answers Vorpal Spikes, which trigger off his autos.

core.why: Highest-sample core path (33.8% pick, 48% WR) — the armor shred keeps your Q/W poke relevant as Cho'Gath stacks HP off Feast kills.
Pairs with Black Cleaver in the same build path — the HP and tenacity let you survive Rupture-into-Feral Scream engages while you kite.
Completes the top measured path — scaling resistances match Cho'Gath's late-game HP stacking so he can't just out-tank you.

runes.keystoneWhy: The dominant measured page (33.6% pick, 57.5% WR) — the stacking vulnerability from ranged autos and Echoing Flames procs pairs with poking him from 490-800 range instead of sitting in melee.

summoners.why: Overwhelmingly the measured choice (77.3% pick, 51.1% WR) — Ignite punishes his Carnivore healing off minion and monster kills and secures the solo kill the data says you're favored to get.

playing.title: Never facetank Rupture
playing.detail: Cho'Gath's Q (Rupture, 950 range, 9s cooldown) is a ground-targeted cast — sidestep it. If you eat it, immediately back off instead of continuing to trade, since he'll follow with free Vorpal Spikes autos while you're slowed.

playing.title: Poke from 490-800, not melee
playing.detail: Fight him with Q (Corrosive Charge) and E (Disdain) and let W (Purge) finish from 490 range. Vorpal Spikes only hits in front of him at essentially melee range, so staying outside that radius removes his entire on-hit damage source.

playing.title: Use E's shield to eat Feral Scream
playing.detail: Disdain shields you while it charges, so timing an engage through his W (Feral Scream, 300 range cone, 13s cooldown, silences) lets you absorb the silence instead of eating it defenseless.

playing.title: Threaten the execute from level 6
playing.detail: R (Fear Beyond Death, 2500 range) impales and can execute him once he drops below the health threshold — play trades knowing any overextension past mid-HP can just end the fight outright.

playing.title: Starve his Feast stacks
playing.detail: Every kill from R (Feast) permanently grows his max HP up to 6 stacks. Don't let him freely eat low-HP minions or jungle camps uncontested, since each stack is what eventually closes the gap he's behind in lane.

playing.title: Press before his items online
playing.detail: Your Black Cleaver into Sterak's Gage spike comes online before his tank items catch up — look for all-ins in the level 6-11 window rather than waiting, since the matchup evens out once he's stacked and itemized.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the ability breakdowns, timing windows, and tactical reasoning are my own read on top of that data.
